Quick technical readout based on the usage sheet Emma shared:

- Batching: For search enrichment (avg 320 tokens), batching gives modest GPU utilization gains — expect 1.2–1.6x cost improvement if you accept a 15–25ms p95 added latency. For nightly summarization (1,800 tokens), batching is highly effective and will drop per-token cost materially because kernel overheads amortize over long sequences.

- KV caching: Your long-session behavior benefits from shard-local KV caches pinned to customer affinity. Warmup for a new cache cluster is data-dependent; plan for ~48–72 hours to reach >80% prefix hit for stable personas. We can implement an early-eviction policy for pilot to reduce memory pressure (tradeoff: slightly lower hit-rate).

- Quantization: We recommend evaluating two quant profiles: 
  a) Q4_HPT (aggressive) — best cost reduction (~30–40%) but test carefully for subtle tokenization drift on small prompts (search enrichment).
  b) Q5_SAFE (balanced) — ~15–20% cost reduction with near-zero quality regression on longer summarization tasks.

Operational caveats:
- When toggling quantization mid-run, run a split-traffic canary to watch hallucination/precision metrics (we can wire in your eval prompt-set).
- Autoscaling: Prefers node-granularity scaling for predictable KV cache locality; otherwise warmup losses diminish savings.

I’ll attach a short runbook and a script to collect eval prompts and compute simple ROUGE/EM-like deltas so procurement can see quality preservation.

— Priyom
